assertions.text: Table columns represent the method's public inputs (applicant type, age, claim count) and observable outputs (decision, premium) — not internal state
assertions.evidence: Columns: Applicant Type | Age | Claims | Status? | Premium? (public inputs/outputs only)

assertions.text: No column is named after private fields or internal variables. The test treats the method as a black box.
assertions.evidence: No hasActivePolicy, internalRiskScore, or riskScore columns. Only Status? and Premium?

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column is 'Scenario' with values like 'Renewal with no claims', 'High risk score'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — not code identifiers
Scenario names describe conditions — not outcomes
assertions.evidence: 'Renewal with no claims', 'High risk score', 'Standard applicant approved' describe input conditions

assertions.text: Table has at least one column name ending with '?'
Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method bodies: assertEquals calls only. No if/switch statements present.
Second method has @Description before @TableTest, but no consistent ordering. First method lacks @Description/@DisplayName.

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title
assertions.evidence: Methods named 'determinesApplicationOutcome' and 'calculatesPremiumForApprovedApplications' are descriptive camelCase titles

assertions.text: If @Description is present and longer than one line, it uses a text block, not string concatenation. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description present is single-line short text: 'Applicant type is NEW for all rows.'

assertions.text: Multiple tables are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table
assertions.evidence: Two @TableTest methods: routing (determinesApplicationOutcome) and premium calculation (calculatesPremiumForApprovedApplications)

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations
assertions.evidence: First table: 5 rows covering routing paths. Second table: 4 rows (age boundary + claims variation). No combinatorial explosion.

assertions.text: Decision logic and premium calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: determinesApplicationOutcome tests Status?; calculatesPremiumForApprovedApplications tests Premium?

assertions.text: Test method body does not recompute internal formulas. Only calls public API and asserts on return values.
assertions.evidence: Method bodies call evaluateApplication() and assert on result.getStatus()/getPremium(). No risk score arithmetic in test.

assertions.text: @Description explains purpose/context — not internal formulas or implementation details
assertions.evidence: Response verification table shows formulas: 'riskScore = age/10 + claims*15' and 'Premium = 100 + riskScore×2' — internals exposed outside @Description but conceptually outside method body

assertions.text: Approval decision table covers the rejection boundary: 5 claims triggers rejection, 4 claims results in approval. Senior vs non-senior (64 vs 65) visible.
assertions.evidence: First table shows 5 claims → REJECTED, but lacks 4-claims row. No age 64 vs 65 comparison in routing table.

assertions.text: Approved premium table covers boundary effects: 0-vs-1 claim impact and age 64-vs-65 threshold
assertions.evidence: Second table rows: '64|0|112.0' vs '65|0|221.0' (age threshold); claims vary (0 and 2) showing impact.
